chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ibrahim from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Muhrim (person in Ihram) may shake off all insects/creatures from himself except for lice, for they are part of his body; and if he wishes to move a louse from one place to another, it does not harm him.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.مِنْ جَسَدِهِ: Part of his body (implying they are not considered separate entities to be removed)

ai.seo_question: What insects can a person in Ihram shake off without breaking their ritual state?
ai.summary: In the context of Ihram regulations, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between external pests and integral body parts, ruling that lice are exempt from the prohibition of removal because they are considered 'from the body' (min jasadih). This specific exemption highlights the juristic principle that minor, attached organisms do not constitute a breach of the sacred state, allowing pilgrims to manage them without incurring penalty or invalidating their ritual status.
